A besieged castle's battlements crumbling under the assault, defenders flung from the walls, towers cracking and catching fire, archers loosing a futile volley.
A massed army on the field breaking in panic, ranks scattering, banners falling, shields raised uselessly against the descending flame.
A rival dragon mid-clash, wings torn and bleeding, jaws snapping back, locked talon-to-talon with the attacker in the smoke-filled sky.
A phalanx of knights with shields raised, the formation buckling under searing heat, steel glowing red, men stumbling backward from the wall of fire.
A fleet of ships in a harbor burning mast to keel, sailors leaping into the water, rigging collapsing, masts toppling in cascades of sparks.
A fortified gatehouse split by a direct strike, the portcullis twisted from its housing, stones raining into the courtyard below, guards fleeing in every direction.
A wizard's tower firing back with spells, bolts of lightning cracking against scales, the mage silhouetted in the window hurling a blinding counterstrike through the smoke.
A column of cavalry dissolving into chaos, horses rearing and bolting, riders thrown, the road ahead consumed in a rolling curtain of orange flame.
A city's burning rooftops collapsing inward, streets choked with fleeing citizens, smoke billowing in black columns, whole districts swallowed by the spreading conflagration.
Siege-engines and catapults reduced to splinters, their crews scattered and burning, throwing arms snapping apart mid-volley, ammunition exploding in sympathetic chain-detonation across the field.
A defending ballista-crew scrambling to reload, their weapon's frame catching fire, one man still cranking the winch even as the shadow descends overhead.
A hero standing alone with a raised sword, refusing to break, the blade glowing white-hot in the inferno, the figure braced against the onrushing storm of flame.
A drawbridge crowded with retreating soldiers, the timbers igniting beneath their boots, men falling into the moat below, the far bank already engulfed.
A war-elephant formation stampeding in terror, mahouts losing control, the animals scattering through their own infantry lines, howdahs ablaze and tumbling free.
A stone watchtower cracking from base to parapet, the bell inside tolling one final peal before the whole structure folds inward in a cloud of dust and fire.
A supply convoy of wagons exploding in sequence, barrels of pitch catching and rocketing skyward, the road buried under burning wreckage for a half-mile in each direction.
A shield-wall of infantry holding grimly, the front rank already scorched, second-rank men pushing forward to replace them, spears leveled against a target that ignores them entirely.
A naval flagship listing hard to port, its gun-deck blown open, the admiral still standing on the burning quarterdeck shouting orders no one can hear anymore.
A mountain fortress carved into the cliff-face, its outer balconies sheared away, the garrison trapped behind collapsed tunnels, smoke pouring from every arrow-slit.
A mercenary pike-square refusing to break, veterans locking shields overhead in a tortoise formation, the canvas above them burning, steam rising from superheated metal.
A second dragon circling defensively, younger and smaller, breathing its own fire in a desperate screen, wings beating hard to gain altitude before the larger beast closes the gap.
A bridge packed with retreating civilians and soldiers alike, the central arch cracking under the heat, stone blocks dropping into the river below in slow, terrible succession.
A trebuchet crew launching a desperate last volley, the projectile sailing wide, the machine's counterweight already ablaze, the crew sprinting away through ankle-deep burning grass.
A royal war-tent in the center of the battlefield, pennants igniting, armored bodyguards forming a ring outward with raised shields, the commander within still shouting commands.
A church tower converted to a signal station, its beacon fire swallowed by something far larger, the flagman still waving his arms as the stones beneath his feet begin to glow.
